caveat: The draft model is actively changing; types.json embeds source_sha256 fdc4dc15e99fa60fd84db10b3debb9e6695de85ccbbbfed63390755129bf9c2e, not the observed Lean hash above. Its historical theorem signatures also differ from current HistoricalStep. No inference of a coherent build or final review applies. Restore revision zero/fresh report, raw intent versus checked frame, cross-ID disjointness and field multiplicity are already being resolved separately; recheck them against the eventual frozen artifacts.

findings.topic: Source elaboration and nominal identity are still an unimplemented trust boundary
findings.evidence: r4 requires complete source-to-IR before command expansion, exact predicate calls and field IDs, yet permits AST associative normalization and the observed pinned parser inserts NOOP wrappers, field domain restrictions and expanded command formulas. The spike exercised parser acceptance, not structural reconstruction or preservation of user-authored occurrences.
findings.resolution: Freeze a per-tag bidirectional concrete-syntax/AST elaboration table with explicit treatment of parentheses, implicit field qualification/domain restriction, binders, call nodes, declaration scope and original command targets. Establish alpha-bijections over declaration/binder identities and ordered trees, including AND/OR flattening with defined reconstruction, and exact names/options/multiplicities. Generated printer output must re-elaborate for every valid supported IR; arbitrary source that cannot be unambiguously re-elaborated must remain TEXT_ONLY or be rejected as specified, never synthesize a supported graph. Differential fixtures must cover nested scopes, same-looking occurrences, all 23 tags, predicate references, all declaration kinds, zero and multiple commands, associativity and precedence, and parser error paths. Parser acceptance by itself is not correspondence.

findings.topic: Exact nominal schema versus Alloy static type and set-valued calls
findings.evidence: The checker requires exact nominal columns, while Alloy's parser resolves relation types and may normalize or discard declared expression information; disjoint signatures and empty intersections can produce parser types whose treatment is not specified. The spike parses set-valued tuple parameters but does not check binary call argument semantics or actual solver results. Positive syntax for tuple set fields is not proof of preserved cardinality.
findings.resolution: Define schema as derivation from named stable declaration references and explicit operators, not as an unchecked cast from parser Type. Require both full parser acceptance and independent derivation of the exact schema, and specify rejection when Alloy type simplification or resolution is inconsistent or ambiguous. Add positive/negative parser and solver fixtures for unary and multi-column set arguments, wrong arity/column ordering, empty and nonempty relations, same-named shadowing, join endpoint mismatch, and n-ary field membership. For field multiplicities prove by small bounded Alloy queries that one/lone/some constrain each owner separately and set tuple ranges admit arbitrary tuples; tuple one/lone/some are rejected by the closed checker. Explicitly retain solver semantics and adapter correspondence outside Lean trust unless proved.

findings.topic: TEXT_ONLY accepted analysis lacks selectable command identity
findings.evidence: TEXT_ONLY stores no module IR or block graph, while analyze requires commandId of an IR command belonging to the accepted revision. The worker currently enumerates parser commands by index. No TEXT_ONLY command identity, selection response, duplicate-label handling or freshness binding is defined.
findings.resolution: Define bounded immutable parser-derived command descriptors separate from IR for TEXT_ONLY, bound to exact artifact, policy and source bytes; specify opaque server-issued occurrence identity or deterministic index plus exact validation and duplicate-label behavior. Analyze resolves and rechecks that identity against the accepted artifact, including empty/no-command source, policy changes and stale artifact, without inventing graph or CorpusPair. Alternatively explicitly make TEXT_ONLY analysis unavailable and reconcile this with inherited A4 and G2/G3 requirements rather than silently weakening them.

findings.topic: Trivia anchors and locations lack complete representation
findings.evidence: Occurrence records require nodeId and expression/operator/reference/binder roles, but comments can attach to signatures, fields, parameter declarations, facts, assertions, commands, closing braces and otherwise empty module boundaries; draft creation has no expression nodes. Source comments may also contain characters that affect columns. The draft says missing position may be unavailable yet accepted BLOCK_SUPPORTED requires maps, without a concrete representation or commit rule.
findings.resolution: Specify closed anchors for declaration IDs, parameter/binder IDs, module boundaries and orphan bucket, plus precise comment token byte interval, half-open convention, tie and copy/move/delete semantics; preserve every comment once except authorized copies. Define explicit unavailable-location representation and whether it blocks block projection, never encode guessed offsets as valid. Test declarations with no bodies, between siblings, EOF, multiline comments, nested spans, supplementary characters, tabs and CRLF with both file and string parser entry points. A lexer must classify only actual comment tokens, not comment-like text inside other syntax.

findings.topic: Formal registry, oracle scope and decoder refinement
findings.evidence: The currently observed types.json hash is stale relative to Lean source. Only infer_sig and infer_var have general soundness/completeness; finite Typed witnesses demonstrate selected instances, not a total validator or full 23-tag differential oracle. Abstract parser admission and checked-frame assumptions cannot prove Java/TypeScript adapters, forest decoding, or database isolation.
findings.resolution: At freeze regenerate and machine-verify exact Lean source/theorem registry hashes, compile with the pinned toolchain twice cleanly, and obtain six independent reviews of those exact frozen inputs. Register proofs and meaningful acceptance/denial witnesses per case. Either prove a total infer/validation soundness theorem for the claimed oracle scope, including all output schema bounds and call arguments, or restrict oracle claims to explicitly enumerated witnessed vectors and report unproved cases. Model raw decoded intent separately from remapping and checked artifact, including endpoint route/key/direction binding. Treat database transitions, reaping, parsing, source identity and adapters as trust plus runtime differential tests; do not claim Lean verifies them.

findings.topic: Runtime admission and SQL feasibility must be evidenced without changing the trusted gateway
findings.evidence: The successful parser spike required an 8 GiB virtual-address cap after failures at 1 and 2 GiB; the r4 production contract requires 2 GiB and reuses launcher isolation. The plan also requires every document migration, RLS, transaction, recovery and test query through the frozen SQLeanParser path; no exercised evidence establishes that its current allowlist supports the proposed DDL and transaction operations.
findings.resolution: Before claiming runtime readiness, exercise the exact existing launcher and reference host at the frozen resource ceiling, including concurrent work and forced failure; a startup failure is availability, not a reason to silently enlarge the bound. Catalog every required SQL statement and transaction operation, verify them through the pinned SQLeanParser proxy and prove rollback/unknown/recovery behavior in integration tests. If a required statement is denied, treat it as a blocker and follow separate controlled gateway-change review; never create a direct PostgreSQL fallback. All Java/TypeScript callables must satisfy the requested documentation and 30-line limit, checked mechanically on the final changed source. Commercial deployment remains NO_GO until separately cleared.
